title: Black Light FTL Sectional Infrastructure Dependency Topology Registry
purpose: Represent large-vessel safety infrastructure as explicit service graphs so local failures propagate only through physically connected power, cooling, command, recovery, hydraulic, dielectric, metabolic and reference paths rather than through one vessel-wide readiness scalar.

designIntentSource.title: The different lightspeed methods
designIntentSource.scope: Drive-specific safety lookahead, emergency de-transit, increasing but imperfect redundancy, gravity-sensitive failure and physically defensible engineering mathematics.

mathematicalModel.pathAvailability: For service path p, A_p = min(A_source, min_e A_e).
mathematicalModel.bestServiceAvailability: A_s = max_p A_p over physically connected source-to-section paths. This is a deterministic widest-path bottleneck measure, not a probability.
mathematicalModel.pathLatency: tau_p = sum_e tau_e. Among paths whose bottleneck availability equals the selected best availability within tolerance, use the minimum latency as the service-response latency.
mathematicalModel.channelReadiness: r_section,channel = min(r_local, A_service) for each declared required service.
mathematicalModel.kOfNGroup: For a safety group requiring k of n members, group readiness is the kth-largest member readiness; group latency is the kth-smallest finite latency among members meeting the readiness floor.
mathematicalModel.aggregateReadiness: Installation channel readiness is the minimum of all declared mandatory group readiness values for that channel; undeclared channels retain incoming readiness.
mathematicalModel.controlSpan: Pi_c = L_c/(v_c*tau_r). Sectional topology changes which regions remain reachable and how quickly, not the external spacetime field.

profiles.description: Generic graph semantics for large installations. It provides no vessel layout, race-specific topology, historical capacities or failure probabilities.
profiles.canonPolicy: Graph layout, supplies, edge availability, latency and redundancy groups must come from named engineering evidence, measured state, or explicitly labeled simulation input.

technologyEmbodiments.guard: Examples are engineering embodiments, not claims that every terrestrial vessel uses this exact architecture.
Ar'nock topology may constrain machinery embodiment but does not establish an FTL family or unsourced numeric performance.
Mur'rek machinery evidence remains family-unresolved; sectional dependencies do not normalize the phrase gravitic slipstream into a consolidated family ID.

runtimeRules: Never infer an edge merely because two systems share a functional label; graph connectivity must be supplied by authority, measurement or labeled simulation state.
Widest-path availability is deterministic service reachability, not reliability probability.
Serial path latency is additive; parallel-path redundancy does not make latency negative or erase propagation delay.
A section isolated from a required service receives zero availability for that service.
k-of-n safety groups must declare k explicitly; do not assume all sections are mandatory or mutually redundant.
Sectional degradation may preserve or worsen incoming readiness but may not improve it without a separately sourced repair/calibration authority.
External gravity, transit-family identity and fictional hazard existence remain upstream and unchanged.
canonGuards: No topology record creates a transit-family assignment.
No path availability value is a historical failure probability.
No disconnected section proves an exotic FTL hazard exists; it proves only that declared infrastructure support is unavailable.
Race/species identity constrains possible embodiment, not universal layout or performance.
Simulation layouts and coefficients remain labeled PROPOSED_ENGINEERING_MODEL.
